title: 5 things to know about Lee Jae-wook, the star of Netflix's “Dead-End Job” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao October 30, 2026 Lee Jae-wook is back on Netflix just in time for Halloween, taking on a part-time job that's far more terrifying than it sounds. In the new mystery-horror series "Dead-End Job," he plays Hyeok-jun, a debt-ridden young man who discovers a mysterious employment agency offering jobs that pay 50 times the minimum hourly wage. But the tempting offer comes with a deadly catch, as each assignment turns into a nightmare. Known for "Alchemy of Souls," "Extraordinary You" and "Dear Hongrang," here are five things to know about the actor 
 He worked various part-time jobs before becoming an actor
 Photo: Netflix
 As it turns out, Lee Jae-wook has something in common with his Dead-End Job character. Long before becoming an actor, he worked various part-time jobs, from serving customers at fast-food restaurants to washing cars. In a 2024 interview, he revealed that while earning money was part of the motivation, he also enjoyed trying his hand at different things, although repetitive routines would eventually bore him. Perhaps that's part of what drew him to acting, a career that allows him to step into different lives and experience something new with every role.
 He landed his debut role on his very first audition
 Photo: tvN
 Lee's acting career got off to a surprisingly quick start. While studying theatre and film at Chung-Ang University, he landed the role of Marco Han in the 2018 drama Memories of the Alhambra , starring Hyun Bin and Park Shin-hye, on his very first audition. Despite landing the part, he admitted being so intimidated by the production's scale that he actually asked the director not to cast him. He later joined Hyun Bin's agency, VAST Entertainment, before parting ways in 2021, and went on to gain wider recognition through Extraordinary You and Alchemy of Souls .

 He is close friends with Rowoon and Ahn Hyo-seop
 Photo: Instagram@jxxvvxxk
 Lee Jae-wook is also part of a popular trio of tall K-drama heartthrobs, alongside Rowoon and Ahn Hyo-seop. He first met Rowoon while filming Extraordinary You in 2019 and later became friends with Ahn through him. In a 2022 interview, Lee shared that the three often get together for drinks and conversations about everything from life to their careers. And their friendship goes beyond casual catch-ups. In 2021, Lee even sent a coffee truck to support Ahn on the set of his historical drama Lovers of the Red Sky .
 He loves cooking and has a surprisingly big appetite
 Photo: Instagram@jxxvvxxk
 Away from the cameras, Lee Jae-wook is quite the foodie. Despite his model frame, the actor reportedly has an impressive appetite and can eat as many as five or six hamburgers in one sitting. But his love for food doesn't stop at eating. He also enjoys cooking and has even taken cooking classes to sharpen his skills. When he's at home, he likes experimenting with different recipes and preparing his own meals. And when he's not in the kitchen, he keeps active with hobbies such as swimming, skiing and cycling.
 He officially made his singing debut in 2026
 Acting isn't Lee Jae-wook's only talent. In August 2024, he impressed audiences with his cover of Park Jae-jung's “Let's Say Goodbye” on The Seasons: Zico's Artist , after Zico personally invited him upon hearing him sing at a private gathering. The performance became a YouTube sensation, reportedly attracting around 10 million views. In June 2026, Lee officially made his singing debut with Shadow , a two-track single album produced by 2AM's Lim Seul-ong. Featuring “The Season Everyone Passes Through”, which he helped write and compose, the project was prepared as a special gift for fans.
